rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a compositional substitution (Mo replaced by V), whereas the hidden target uses thermomechanical processing (cold rolling and annealing) without changing composition. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room-temperature compressive loading, while the hidden target uses room-temperature tensile testing. Both are room-temperature mechanical tests, but the loading mode (compression vs. tension) and the processing conditions (as-cast vs. rolled/annealed) differ substantially.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced electronegativity mismatch and bonding anisotropy to enhance dislocation mobility, while the hidden target relies on work hardening, dislocation accumulation, texture, and subsequent recovery/recrystallization. These are different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved plasticity with strength near 1719 MPa in compression, whereas the hidden target reports tensile strength changes (increase with rolling, decrease with annealing) and elongation changes, with no compressive data and a different baseline strength.
